name: Stargaze
description: Look at the top [N] cards of your library. Put [Y] of them into your hand and the rest into your graveyard. You lose X life.
assumptions: The `X` in node E's `qty:X` (life loss) is the same `X` paid for the spell's `{X}` in its mana cost — there's no other value named `X` anywhere on the card, and no `:=`/`=` binding formally ties them together, so this is an inference from shared naming rather than a derived fact.

Read `cond:dig` on C/D as a "look at cards from the library, then split them into hand and graveyard" effect (Fact-or-Fiction-style), rather than a targeted tutor for a specific card type — consistent with `thing: any` and the absence of any `target` flag or named subtype criterion.
Treated C and D as two parts of one single library look-through (bound together by "remainder" on D), not two independent, separately-sized library actions.
couldNotDerive: The total number of cards looked at/dug through the library. Only that some (`Y`) go to hand (C) and the rest go to the graveyard (D, `remainder`) — no node fixes the total.
The numeric value of `Y` itself (how many cards land in the caster's hand) — it's named but never assigned a number by any registry entry or binding.

Whether the caster chooses which looked-at cards go to hand vs. graveyard, or whether the split is fixed/positional (e.g., "the top Y" automatically) — the schema's `target` flag doesn't cover this kind of internal choice, so the nodes don't settle it.
Supertype and rarity (rarity explicitly withheld in the packet; supertype absent from the self registry's type line).
notes: Second attempt, after both stated translator fixes. Confirmed both landed correctly in this regenerated packet: (1) node C's `to` field now reads "hand" (the previous attempt's hardcoded-"exile" default is gone) — matches real Forge semantics where an unset `DestinationZone$` on Dig defaults to Hand; (2) `DestinationZone2$ Graveyard` is now represented as node D, a genuine sibling of C under root A in `flow.steps["A"]` (`["B","C","D"]`), correctly modeling the two-pile split as two separate move nodes instead of collapsing to one. Real card (forge-model/data/stargaze.txt): `Dig | DigNum$ Y | ChangeNum$ X | DestinationZone2$ Graveyard`, SVar Y:Count$xPaid/Twice, SVar X:Count$xPaid, SubAbility DBLoseLife (LifeAmount$ X). Oracle: "Look at twice X cards from the top of your library. Put X cards from among them into your hand and the rest into your graveyard. You lose X life." The examiner's reconstruction gets the full shape right this time — single library look-through that splits into a hand pile and a graveyard 'remainder' pile, followed by losing life equal to the spell's own paid X — correctly omitted node B (self, stack->gy) as ordinary post-resolution zone travel rather than printed text, and invented nothing: it left both the hand-pile size and the total look-count as explicit placeholders rather than guessing numbers. Its one substantive assumption (E's qty:X = the cast's own {X}) is in fact correct against the real card (SVar X:Count$xPaid backs both ChangeNum and LifeAmount). The residual gap is exactly the one flagged in advance as deliberately deferred: node C's flag names the hand-destination quantity `Y`, but the real script's `Y` is actually the *look* count (DigNum = Count$xPaid/Twice = twice X) while the *hand* count is `X` (ChangeNum = Count$xPaid) — i.e. the packet has the right two sibling moves and the right two named variables (X, Y) sitting on the right nodes, but carries no SVar-level formula tying Y = 2*X, and doesn't disambiguate which of the two named counts is the 'look' quantity vs. the 'hand' quantity. That's the ChangeNum-vs-DigNum split and the X/Y-to-mana-cost-variable binding the task called out up front as known/still-not-fully-derivable — not a decomposition bug, not a schema expressiveness gap, and not agent misinterpretation (the agent correctly refused to guess rather than picking a number). Everything else — mana cost, type line, the dig-then-split-then-lose-life shape, and the absence of any invented specifics — matches the real card.
